title: Ok digit sum eight
statement: How many four-digit numbers use only the digits $1$, $2$ and $3$ (repeats allowed) and have digit sum $8$?
hints: Lower every digit by one so the digits become $0$, $1$, $2$.
Split into cases by how many digits equal $2$ after the shift.
solution: Subtract $1$ from each digit: we want four values from $\{0,1,2\}$ with sum $4$. Sort by the number of $2$s. Two $2$s and two $0$s: $\binom42 = 6$ ways. One $2$, two $1$s and one $0$: $4\cdot 3 = 12$ ways. No $2$s: four $1$s, $1$ way. Three or more $2$s would exceed the sum. The total is $6 + 12 + 1 = 19$.
check_program:
from itertools import product
print(sum(1 for t in product([1, 2, 3], repeat=4) if sum(t) == 8))
